statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-53057 is an Oracle Java SE Security (java.security) issue from the October 2025 Critical Patch Update, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.9 by JDK-8360937 ("Enhance certificate handling"). The fix changes how X.509 distinguished names are parsed and rendered (sun.security.util.DerValue and sun.security.x509.AVA): before 21.0.9, BMPString values containing surrogate characters were accepted, and the RFC 2253 string forms decoded PrintableString, IA5String, T61String and BMPString values as UTF-8 regardless of their encoding. The flaw is in OpenJDK code, so every OpenJDK build (Temurin, Corretto, Zulu, Oracle) before 21.0.9 is affected. The Docker image versions were read from each published image with java -version: 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.8+9, 5.0.2 and 5.0.3 ship 21.0.9+10, and later images ship 21.0.10 or newer. The Windows installer versions were read from the install4j jreBundle setting at each release tag: 5.0.0 through 5.0.4 bundle jdk-21.0.8+9, and 5.1.0 and later bundle 21.0.10 or newer.
statements.impact_statement: The Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 Docker images and the 5.0.0 through 5.0.4 Windows installers ship an affected runtime (Temurin 21.0.8); Docker images from 5.0.2 and installers from 5.1.0 ship Temurin 21.0.9 or newer and include the fix. The flawed code is present in that runtime; this assessment is that an attacker cannot exploit it through Liquibase Secure. Before 21.0.9, X500Principal.getName() in the RFC 2253 and canonical forms decoded name values as UTF-8 regardless of their ASN.1 string type, so a certificate name could render as text it does not contain. Liquibase Secure only acts as a TLS client, so the only certificate names it receives from a peer are those of the server certificates it validates. Path validation verifies every signature with the issuing CA's key, so a name can only reach any code in the process that reads it (the JDK's hostname verification, a bundled JDBC driver's own host name check, or Liquibase code) in a certificate signed by a CA the client trusts. Chain building and name constraints compare names in the affected canonical form, but a colliding issuer name only selects a candidate CA whose key must still verify the signature, and a subject that collides into a permitted subtree must still be signed by the constrained CA itself. Exploitation therefore requires a trusted CA to sign a server certificate with a deliberately malformed name. Publicly trusted CAs may not issue such certificates under the CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements, and an attacker able to get a trusted private CA to sign a certificate can already issue a valid one for the host, so the flaw adds nothing to that position. The JDK's own hostname verification reads SAN entries and the CN through DerValue.getAsString(), which decodes correctly. Liquibase code reads a certificate name only in DaticalTrueLicenseService, to display the holder of a license file that Liquibase signs.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Libraries (core-libs) issue, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.9 by JDK-8359454 ("Enhance String handling"). The Java version was read from each published image with java -version: 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.8+9, 5.0.2 and later ship 21.0.9 or newer. The fix changes a single branch of java.lang.AbstractStringBuilder.insert(int, CharSequence, int, int): the one taken when the inserted sequence is a String and only part of it is inserted. A whole String now goes through the existing putStringAt(int, String) path, which copies the same bytes as the code it replaced, so the behaviour that changed is limited to inserting a sub-range of a String. A bytecode scan of the 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 images found no caller of that form. In the JRE's lib/modules, no class other than StringBuilder, StringBuffer and AbstractStringBuilder references the four-argument insert. Across all jars under /liquibase, including nested jars and the license-tracking application, its only caller is the shaded ICU class CollationIterator$SkippedState in liquibase-checks.jar, which inserts a StringBuilder, not a String. The callers of insert(int, CharSequence), which forwards the whole sequence, are in shaded ICU and the DB2 JDBC driver and insert either a StringBuilder or a whole sequence. The changed code is therefore not executed by Liquibase Secure.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. Oracle Java SE Libraries issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. One candidate, JDK-8382407 (Enhance LDAP Lookups), tightens which object factories a JNDI LDAP lookup may use; the Oracle JDBC driver uses JNDI LDAP to resolve jdbc:oracle:thin:@ldap:// URLs, so a malicious LDAP directory could reach it. Because the fixed code cannot be pinned down and the core libraries are used throughout, this is recorded as affected.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. Liquibase Secure 6.0.0 and earlier images and Windows installers bundle a Temurin 21.0.12.1 JRE whose cacerts still trusts the emSign roots the compromised intermediates chain to. Temurin builds cacerts from Mozilla's root store, which still trusts emSign Root CA - G1, so a Temurin update alone does not remove it. Builds with SECURE-1170 run docker/distrust-emsign.sh on the bundled JRE, which deletes every emSign and Comodo AAA root from cacerts; the JRE version string is unchanged, so scanners still report this CVE for those builds too. Until you upgrade, delete those roots from the bundled JRE's cacerts.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE and OpenJDK (component: HotSpot compiler) affecting OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later, including Java SE 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5 and 27.0.1, 8u511-perf, and the corresponding GraalVM releases. Known as Java4Shell. On x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI, the JIT-compiled java.util.Base64 decoder miscomputes the output length for malformed padded input and writes up to 62 bytes past the end of the output array. An unauthenticated attacker who can send Base64 data to an application's decoder can corrupt the heap, leak heap memory and, with an exploit built for the application, execute code.
statements.action_statement: Liquibase Secure images and Windows installers bundle a Temurin 21 JRE (21.0.13 or earlier) that contains the vulnerable Base64 decoder. No Temurin release with the fix is available yet. Practical exposure is low for inbound attacks. Liquibase is a short-lived command-line process that accepts no inbound connections, and the Base64 data it decodes (license files, changelogs, loadData values) comes from the user. The published server exploits need many crafted requests to one long-running JVM, to warm up the decoder and arrange the heap. The remaining path is outbound: the researchers report a client-side exploit against a Java program that opens a TLS connection to a malicious server, so a run that connects to a database or service an attacker controls or impersonates may be exposed. Applications that embed the Liquibase libraries run on their own Java runtime and are affected through that runtime. Only x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Intel Ice Lake and newer Xeon, AMD Zen 4 and newer) are affected; ARM64 is not.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE JGSS vulnerability. statements.action_statement: Oracle Java SE JSSE (TLS client) vulnerability from the November 2026 security update, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.13.1 by JDK-8393456 (Improve TLS client connections): on a non-anonymous TLS 1.2 cipher suite the client accepted a ServerKeyExchange and ServerHelloDone without the server's Certificate, so a network attacker could complete a handshake without proving the server's identity. Oracle states that this vulnerability applies only to Java deployments that load and run untrusted code and rely on the Java sandbox for security (sandboxed Java Web Start applications or applets), and does not apply to deployments that load and run only trusted code installed by an administrator. Liquibase Secure is a command-line tool that runs only its own code, the extensions and drivers its operator installs, and the operator's changelogs; it does not use the Java sandbox and never runs code from an untrusted source. The image's entrypoint starts the Liquibase launcher, and the tools shipped in the JRE's bin directory besides java (jfr, jrunscript, jwebserver, keytool, rmiregistry) are not run by Liquibase.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE (component: Utility). statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Utility issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update, which the OpenJDK advisory places in core-libs/java.util and which needs a local attacker (AV:L). Of the 21.0.13 fixes, the two that fit are JDK-8384746 (Enhance Preferences) and JDK-8341625 (ZipFile validation of the END header). No class in any Liquibase Secure image from 5.0.1 to 6.0.0, including jars nested in the extensions, uses java.util.prefs, so the Preferences code never runs. The ZIP flaw needs a crafted JAR or ZIP file that Liquibase opens: its own jars, extensions, drivers and changelog archives. An attacker able to write those files on the Liquibase host can already change the changelogs Liquibase runs against the database, which gives far more than this flaw does, so it adds no exposure in the expected deployment environment.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE (component: Networking). Supported versions that are affected include Oracle Java SE 11.0.32.1, 17.0.20.1, 21.0.12.1, 25.0.4.1 and 27, and the corresponding GraalVM releases. statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Networking issue (OpenJDK component core-libs/java.net, Java 11 and later) from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. Liquibase Secure images 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ship Temurin 21 JREs from 21.0.8 to 21.0.12.1, all in Oracle's affected range; images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. The Java 11+ java.net fixes in 21.0.13 are all in the JDK HTTP client (java.net.http): response handling, connections, headers and authentication caching. A scan of every class in the 5.0.1, 5.0.2, 5.1.1 and 5.2.2 images, including jars nested in the extensions, found no use of java.net.http, so those images never run the affected code. In 6.0.0 the only classes that use it are LicenseAccessClient (liquibase-commercial, the Liquibase license service), HttpChecksSettingsFileClient (liquibase-checks, a checks settings URL the operator configures), the Astra SDK's HttpClientWrapper (liquibase-commercial-cassandra, the DataStax Astra API when connecting to Astra), dnsjava's DohResolver (liquibase-gcp-extension, DNS over HTTPS when configured) and jsoup's HttpClientExecutor shaded in snowflake-jdbc (the driver connects only to the Snowflake account the operator configures). Each is an endpoint chosen by the operator and reached over TLS with certificate validation. Exploitation needs one of those trusted endpoints to be malicious or compromised, which is outside the expected deployment environment.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Serviceability issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. Liquibase Secure images 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ship Temurin 21 JREs from 21.0.8 to 21.0.12.1, all in Oracle's affected range; images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. The OpenJDK advisory of 2026-10-20 places this CVE in core-svc (CVE-2026-91374 is the core-svc/tools one), which matches JDK-8385249 (Enhance diagnostic sessions). The October update has two Serviceability fixes: JDK-8384930 (Enhance jstatd), in the jstatd remote monitoring server, and JDK-8385249 (Enhance diagnostic sessions), in the client side of the attach API that tools such as jcmd use to connect to a running JVM. Neither module is in the runtime Liquibase Secure ships: the Temurin 21 JRE in every published image from 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 contains neither the jdk.jstatd nor the jdk.attach module, nor the attach native library, so the fixed code can never run (java --list-modules in every image from 5.0.1 to 6.0.2 lists neither module, $JAVA_HOME/bin has no jstatd or jcmd, and the image has no libattach.so).

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Networking issue in the SOCKS5 client from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. Liquibase Secure images 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ship Temurin 21 JREs from 21.0.8 to 21.0.12.1, all in Oracle's affected range; images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. Oracle's advisory names SOCKS5 as the attack path, and the only SOCKS change in 21.0.13 is JDK-8385260 (Enhance SOCKS5 support), so that is the fix. It is in the JDK's SOCKS socket implementation. That code runs only when a connection goes through a SOCKS proxy, which requires the operator to configure one (the socksProxyHost system property, a driver's SOCKS proxy property, or a proxy selector that returns a SOCKS proxy). Liquibase sets no SOCKS proxy, and the published images set no proxy options in their environment, so the default configuration never reaches the fixed code. An attacker would also need to control or impersonate the configured proxy.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Sound issue (javax.sound). Every published Liquibase Secure image from 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ships a Temurin 21 JRE between 21.0.8 and 21.0.12.1, which is in Oracle's affected range, and that JRE includes the sound library, so the version alone does not rule it out. statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE (component: JSSE) affecting Oracle Java SE 8u511, 11.0.33, 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5 and 27.0.1 and the corresponding GraalVM releases. statements.action_statement: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. Liquibase Secure 6.0.0 and earlier images and Windows installers bundle a Temurin 21.0.12.1 JRE that still trusts the compromised eMudhra intermediates. Builds with SECURE-1170 run docker/distrust-emsign.sh on the bundled JRE, which adds the 48 fingerprints from the upstream fix (JDK-8395142) to lib/security/blocked.certs; the JRE version string is unchanged, so scanners still report this CVE for those builds too. Until you upgrade, add the fingerprints to the bundled JRE's blocked.certs.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE 2D issue (the graphics, imaging and font rendering subsystem). Every published Liquibase Secure image from 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ships a Temurin 21 JRE between 21.0.8 and 21.0.12.1, which is in Oracle's affected range, so the version alone does not rule it out. Images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. Liquibase Secure is a command-line tool that does not render images or fonts or decode untrusted image data. Liquibase's own code references only java.awt.Desktop, which hands a generated report to the local browser after an interactive run and is skipped when Liquibase's headless setting is on. That call passes a file path to the operating system and does no 2D rendering. A scan of the bundled jars for java.awt and javax.imageio references found these other users, none of which Liquibase passes image or font data to: browser-based sign-in helpers in the cloud and JDBC drivers (Desktop only), the H2 and HSQLDB GUI tools, geometry conversion helpers in the Databricks driver and Apache Commons Math, JAXB's image binding (Liquibase's JAXB models have no image fields), and the bundled data redaction library's PDF/image path, which uses ImageIO and Java 2D but is never run because Liquibase Secure calls that library only with plain text.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE ImageIO issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update; Oracle lists 21.0.12.1 as the last affected Java 21 release. The published Liquibase Secure images ship Temurin JRE 21.0.9 (5.0.2, 5.0.3), 21.0.10 (5.1.0, 5.1.1), 21.0.11 (5.2.0, 5.2.1), 21.0.12 (5.2.2) and 21.0.12.1 (6.0.0), so every one of them carries the vulnerable version. statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Lightweight HTTP Server (com.sun.net.httpserver) issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update; Oracle lists 21.0.12.1 as the last affected Java 21 release. The published Liquibase Secure images ship Temurin JRE 21.0.9 (5.0.2, 5.0.3), 21.0.10 (5.1.0, 5.1.1), 21.0.11 (5.2.0, 5.2.1), 21.0.12 (5.2.2) and 21.0.12.1 (6.0.0), so every one of them carries the vulnerable version. Exploitation requires an attacker to send requests to an HTTP server built on that API. Liquibase itself never starts an HTTP server: a source review found no use of com.sun.net.httpserver or any other listening socket in Liquibase code outside its tests, the images declare no exposed ports, and their entrypoint only runs the Liquibase CLI. Three bundled libraries do start a com.sun.net.httpserver listener, to receive the redirect of an interactive browser sign-in: the Microsoft authentication library (Azure interactive sign-in), the Databricks driver's OAuth browser flow and the Snowflake driver's OAuth authorization-code flow. These run only when a user configures one of those sign-in methods (Liquibase's Azure extension itself uses only Azure's default credential chain, which has no interactive browser sign-in). The listener is bound to the loopback interface and lives only while the user completes sign-in, so an attacker would need to send requests from the same machine during that window. Images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. Oracle Java SE JSSE (TLS) certificate validation issue (CWE-295) from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. Liquibase Secure images 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ship Temurin 21 JREs from 21.0.8 to 21.0.12.1, all in Oracle's affected range; images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. Certificate validation runs on every HTTPS and TLS JDBC connection Liquibase makes, and a certificate validation flaw is what an attacker on the network path between Liquibase and its database or service would use, so this is recorded as affected. The impact is limited to low integrity, and exploitation is hard.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later if you use Kerberos authentication. Oracle Java SE JGSS (Kerberos) issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. Unlike the sandbox-only JGSS issues CVE-2026-91463 and CVE-2026-91464, this one can be exploited by supplying data to the Kerberos APIs. Those are supported configurations, so users who enable them are affected; an attacker would need to interfere with the Kerberos exchange, for example from the network path to the KDC or database. Users who do not configure Kerberos never run this code.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Compiler (HotSpot C2 JIT) issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update, affecting Java 11, 17, 21 and later. Liquibase Secure images 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ship Temurin 21 JREs from 21.0.8 to 21.0.12.1, all in Oracle's affected range; images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. Of the two C2 fixes in OpenJDK 21.0.13, JDK-8390400 (Enhance C2 comparisons, which corrects how compiled x86 code returns the old value of a byte or short compare-and-swap) is the one also backported to Java 17, so it matches this CVE's version list. The JIT compiles all code, so the flaw cannot be ruled out by reachability. Exploitation needs an attacker to supply data that drives a specific compiled code path in a long-running service that processes attacker requests. Liquibase Secure is a short-lived command-line process that accepts no inbound connections and processes changelogs and settings supplied by its operator.
